what_it_does: When printing a chip's circuit pattern onto silicon, manufacturers use light to etch features — a process called lithography. At very small sizes, a single exposure of light cannot create all the required features without them blurring into each other, so the pattern must be split across three separate masks (templates), each printed in sequence — this is called Triple Patterning Lithography (TPL). Wires connecting multiple circuit pins must be routed carefully so that neighboring wire segments don't end up on the same mask (a 'color conflict') or require ugly and error-prone overlapping patches called 'stitches'. This paper presents Mr.TPL, a routing method that handles wires connecting more than two pins at once, using novel color-assignment and stitch-reduction algorithms to minimize both types of problems across all three mask layers.
